title: landlord_found_my_channel
display_title: My landlord found my parkour channel and now rent depends on my next upload
beats: My landlord commented on my parkour video from an account with his wife's name on it.
I found out by accident — he liked a video from eight months ago at 3AM.
Two days later he texts me: 'Rent's going up $200 unless you can get me to 10K subscribers by spring.'
I laughed until I realized he wasn't joking — he'd already told the other tenants I run the building's 'official channel.'
He started showing up during my recordings, standing just off camera, coaching me on angles like he built the course himself.
When I finally hit 10K, he posted a video captioned 'my building, my talent' — my face blurred out, his name in the title.
I have the lease, the texts, and forty unlisted videos proving every route was mine.
Reddit, do I expose him to his own tenants, or just move out and let him keep chasing views for a channel that's already dead?
